<description>
Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/5029

Accept unix socket paths as options for `-rpcbind=` (server) and `-rpcconnect=` (bitcoin-cli). Options follow the same pattern as `ipcbind`:

- `=unix` is a magic keyword that means `<datadir>/http.sock`
- `=unix:relative/path` means `<datadir>/relative/path`
- `=unix:/absolute/path` means `/absolute/path`

We delete any existing `http.sock` before calling `bind()` and do not clean up at shutdown.

Because access is handled by the filesystem, `-rpcallowip` is ignored for unix sockets and not required at all if we are *only* binding to unix sockets.

Authentication by username/password/cookie is still required.

A new option `--httpunix` is added to the test framework and added to test_runner for `rpc_bind.py` and `interface_http.py` for CI, but (like `--usecli`) most other tests should also pass with that option. When set, bitcoind is started with `-rpcbind=unix...`which overrides `tcp://localhost` entirely. `AuthProxy` has been extended to connect directly to the unix socket.

Try it out!
```
bitcoind -regtest -rpcbind=unix
bitcoin-cli -regtest -rpcconnect=unix getbestblockhash
```

Refactored code:

Back in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/27375 we added unix socket support but it was isolated to the `Proxy` class. That created a bit of tech debt which we pay off in this PR. Two new classes are implemented:
- `UnixSocketAddr` reflects the `CService` API for generic unix sockets, without bitcoin-p2p-specific attributes
- `SocketAddr` holds a variant of `UnixSocketAddr` and `Cservice` so classes like `Proxy` and `HTTPServer` can operate on an abstract level, with either socket type.
- `CNetAddr` and `CService` are left untouched -- they are somewhat dirty combinations of generic socket classes and bitcoin p2p code, adding unix sockets to those classes wouldn't make sense for bitcoin p2p operations and that's why this design was chosen.

Follow-up suggestions:
- Deduplicate some of the unix socket path resolution code between IPC and HTTP
- On macos the default unix socket buffer size is only ~8k. In the functional tests we have to bump the python client socket buffer up to ~256k or the "throttle" tests will stall on macos. We could apply this socket option on the server side as well, only on macos... requires some bike shedding.
- This option replaces TCP but it does not replace HTTP, there may be a more efficient transport protocol.

Production code and test framework changes designed and authored by my own cranial meatball. Unit tests added by Opus. C++ cleaned up by Fable, security tightened by Kimi-k3 🧠 🤖 🤖 🤖
</description>

### the autopsy

the test case assumes that when the server rejects a request and closes the connection, a client blocked in `sendall()` should wake up on an error. this happens on Linux and over TCP (on all supported platforms), but not on FreeBSD _with unix sockets_. so, a client already blocked in a long `poll()` is not woken up and it waits out its full socket timeout as a result

i tried to reproduce this similar scenario without `bitcoind` i.e. with a plain Python server that never reads and closes after `1` second which caused the client's `sendall()` to time out after `10` seconds across 4 runs in a deterministic way.

reproducer script

```py
import os, socket, threading, time, tempfile

##########
# server
##########
path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "t.sock")
srv = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); srv.bind(path); srv.listen()

def server():
    c, _ = srv.accept()
    time.sleep(1)                      # never read, like bitcoind after rejecting
    c.send(b"HTTP/1.1 413\r\n\r\n")
    c.close()                          # close with unread data pending

threading.Thread(target=server, daemon=True).start()

##########
# client
##########
cli = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); cli.settimeout(10)
cli.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_SNDBUF, 1 << 18)
cli.connect(path)
t = time.time()
try:
    cli.sendall(b"0" * (32 << 20)); print("sendall finished")
except TimeoutError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, e, f"after {time.time()-t:.1f}s")
except Exception as e:
    print("error not expected: ", e)

```

---
`bitcoind` is closing the connection correctly. the issue appears to be that FreeBSD does not wake an already-blocked client in this scenario

**edit**: this behaviour does not manifest on netBSD

[2026-11-02] rc:4447566196 inline on test/functional/test_framework/netutil.py by winterrdog (contributor) (edited 2026-11-02):
on netBSD, this fails with `OSError: [Errno 55] No buffer space available`

the error is caused by setting `SO_SNDBUF` to 256 KiB (`1 << 18`), which netBSD rejects because its default socket buffer limit, `kern.sbmax`, is also 256 KiB. 128 KiB (`1 << 17`) works just fine, and so does 256 KiB _provided_ `kern.sbmax` is raised above 256 KiB

we could just lower `SO_SNDBUF` to 128 KiB (`1 << 17`) so that `interface_http.py --httpunix` passes end to end on netBSD too. the only thing i am not so sure about is whether 128 KiB is enough for the macOS throttle stall that motivated the 256 KiB in the first place

alternatively, we could keep 256 KiB and fall back to 128 KiB on `OSError`, but it would be preferable to just keep this simple _if 128 KiB is enough_

what do you think ?
